sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 9.1% a year from FY2016 to FY2025, rising from $23.7 billion to $51.8 billion [F1][F10][F168].
The path was cyclical rather than steady: revenue fell 58.0% in FY2020 to $13.7 billion, then rose 153.2% in FY2021 and 76.5% in FY2022 to $61.0 billion [F5][D161][F6][D200][F7][D238].
The FY2022 jump came mainly from higher realized commodity prices and higher sales volumes, mostly from the Shell Permian acquisition [P59].
Revenue then fell 20.5% in FY2023 to $48.5 billion and has grown only 4.9% in FY2025 to $51.8 billion, a 3-year CAGR of -5.3% [F8][D274][F10][D342][D844].
Crude oil is the largest line at 66.3% of FY2025 revenue, but it contributed just 0.1pp to FY2025 growth [D551][D553].
The U.S. supplied 79.1% of FY2025 revenue and 5.7pp of growth, while non-U.S. added 2.0pp [D382][D384][D400].
Sales and other operating revenues rose $4.2 billion in 2025 on higher volumes of $6.2 billion, including Marathon Oil volumes, partly offset by lower realized crude prices [P28].
Net income fell 13.6% in FY2025 against 4.9% revenue growth, and EPS fell 18.7% as the diluted share count rose 6.1% [D343][D342][D344][D356].
Cost of revenue grew 11.6% in FY2025, faster than the 4.9% revenue growth [D352][D342].
Net margin of 15.4% in FY2025 sits below the 17.9% window median but far above the -19.8% FY2020 low and the 30.6% FY2022 high [F30][D831][D829][D830].
Net margin fell 3.3pp in FY2025, with cost of revenue at 37.9% of revenue against 36.6% in FY2024 [D351][D326][D292].

DD&A rose $1.9 billion in 2025 on the Marathon Oil acquisition and higher production volumes, and production and operating expenses rose $1.6 billion on the same acquisition plus $216 million of severance [P22][P24].
The effective tax rate rose to 36.9% in FY2025 from 32.4% in FY2024, leaving net margin 15.4% against a 24.4% pre-tax margin [D332][D298][F30][X91][F10].
Operating cash flow of $19.8 billion was 2.48x net income in FY2025, above the 2.07x window median, while operating cash flow fell 1.6% [F59][D333][D855][D346].
The 2025 decline came from lower commodity prices, mostly offset by operations from the 2024 Marathon Oil acquisition [P6].
Operating cash flow was 33.6% of revenue in FY2025, and capex of $10.2 billion in FY2022 was 1.35x D&A [D331][F66][D228].
Free cash flow margin peaked at 24.1% in FY2021 against a 12.2% window median, and stock-based compensation was only 1.7% of operating cash flow in FY2025 [D833][D834][D334].
Cash and investments were $8.1 billion at FY2025, up 13.4%, with a current ratio of 1.30x against a 1.45x window median [D335][D357][F153][D843].
Net cash was -$12.9 billion, or -67.0% of revenue, in FY2020, the last year the pack reports it; long-term debt is not reported after FY2020, so later net-cash figures are omitted [D155][D156][F157].

In 2025 the company spent $12.6 billion on capital and investments, $5.0 billion on buybacks, $4.0 billion on dividends and $0.9 billion on debt retirement, partly offset by $3.2 billion of asset sales [P7].

Buybacks plus dividends of $9.0 billion were 46% of operating cash flow, and return on average equity of 12.4% ranked in the 33rd percentile of six energy peers against a 14.9% median [P31][D341][D852][D853].
Revenue in the table is a later recast for every year: FY2025 shows $51.8 billion against $58.9 billion as first reported [F10][X10].
Growth and margin comparisons that mix a recast year with a first-reported year are not like-for-like, so the 9.1% CAGR should be read with that caveat [F168].
Long-term debt is not reported before FY2017 or after FY2020, and short-term investments are missing in FY2021 [X204][F157][X183][X184].
Net cash and debt-based rankings are therefore only available for FY2017 to FY2020 and cannot be extended to the latest year [D32][D155].
Revenue fell 20.5% in FY2023 to $48.5 billion [F8][D274].
The decline was price-led and the top line has not recovered to the FY2022 level, leaving earnings exposed to another commodity downcycle [F7][F10].
Whether FY2026 revenue exceeds the FY2025 level of $51.8 billion, confirming the current 4.9% growth trend, in the FY2026 10-K [F10][D342].
Whether net margin holds above the 17.9% window median or falls toward the 15.4% FY2025 level, in the FY2026 10-K [D831][F30].
Whether operating cash flow stays above the FY2025 $19.8 billion level, against the $20.1 billion FY2024 figure, in the FY2026 10-K [F59][F58].
